conviction_note: The Q3 number was effectively pre-announced (around 17% cc guided on 22 Sep, eight days before quarter end, and consensus CHF 931m / +17.2% sits on it), so the print turns on the Q4 guide that the low-20% FY range implies (about 15-23% cc) and on early 2027 commentary. Peer evidence is mixed: Deckers/HOKA cut, Nike and Adidas running strong. The stock is up about 40% from its post-Q2 low with calls slightly bid. The findings sum to -0.6, and the scaled number is (2x0.48-1)x10 = -0.4. The two agree that this is close to a non-result on direction, with a large two-way move: the name moved +18% and -20% on its last two guidance changes.
bar: Company guide: Q3 2026 constant-currency net sales growth of around 17% (Investor Day release, 2026-09-22, https://finviz.com/news/394033/on-enters-next-chapter-unveils-strategy-to-redefine-what-a-sportswear-brand-can-be-alongside-2029-financial-targets). Consensus: revenue CHF 931.06m, +17.2% YoY, EPS CHF 0.346 (futunn preview, https://news.futunn.com/en/post/1003476745/earnings-preview-on-holding-to-report-financial-results-pre-market, snippet only). USD consensus: $1.14bn and EPS $0.50, whisper $0.52 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-03, https://finviz.com/news/414150/on-holdings-wholesale-reset-faces-its-test-as-q3-growth-dips-below-15). MarketBeat has $1.11bn and $0.4654 (https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/11/09/on-onon-set-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday.html). Chartmill's CHF 947.64m is an outlier. FY: low-20% cc, gross margin >=65%, adj. EBITDA 19.5-20.0%, CHF 3.47-3.56bn at 11 Aug spot rates; FY consensus $4.33bn against a $4.28-4.39bn range. The bar is sourced to a company guide plus agreeing estimates, so sizes are not capped for the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 5.93% of float, 19.8m shares, 4.9 days to cover, data through August 2026 (https://equibles.com/stocks/onon/shortinterest); MarketBeat had 3.15% on 2026-05-29. Neither is crowded, so a squeeze is not a material mechanism. 25-delta skew is -2.18 vol points, meaning calls are slightly bid and the market leans to upside, but mildly. P/C OI 0.75. Event-implied move 8.77% (straddle 9.48%). The stock is at $37.07: +4.36% over 5 days, +4.87% over 20 days, +26% from the $29.39 Investor Day close, +40% from the $26.37 post-Q2 low, and still -26.8% from its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Q3 sales are essentially pre-announced. On guided Q3 net sales growth of around 17% cc on 22 Sep 2026, eight days before quarter end. Consensus of CHF 931m (+17.2% YoY on Q3-25's CHF 794.4m) sits on that guide, and the Q3 revenue line is expected to land inside a figure the company already gave.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2-26 (11 Aug 2026): a revenue miss of CHF 850.3m against about CHF 878-881m, together with a FY cut, gave -20.3%. Q3-25 (12 Nov 2025): a beat of CHF 794.4m against CHF 763.8m plus a FY raise gave about +18% (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/on-holding-stock-soars-18-after-company-raises-full-year-outlook-cites-strong-momentum-into-holidays-213711770.html). Both moves came with a guidance change, so the reported-quarter line alone is not isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced, which is the point: consensus equals the guide. A Q3 sales surprise large enough to matter would need the company to have mis-guided a quarter that was 92% complete. This finding argues for a smaller reported-quarter contribution, not for a sign.
findings.independence: The consensus figure (futunn, CHF 931.06m, +17.2%) is a different source that agrees with the guide. The Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/414150/on-holdings-wholesale-reset-faces-its-test-as-q3-growth-dips-below-15) says the Street has 'accepted the reset'.

findings.finding: The reiterated FY guide of low-20% cc growth implies Q4 cc growth of roughly 15% (FY at 20%) to 23% (FY at 22%), against about 17% in Q3. Basis: FY25 CHF 3.01bn, H1-26 +24.0% cc on CHF 1,475.6m, Q3 +17% on CHF 794.4m, so Q4-25 is about CHF 740m. Management said on the Q2 call that Q3 growth would be lower than Q4 and cited a doubled SS27 order book. Narrowing to the low end reads as a cut; holding 21%+ requires a visible Q4 acceleration while the Americas are promotional.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is this name's line. FY cut in Aug 2026: -20.3%. FY raise in Nov 2025: about +18%. First FY26 guide of >=23% cc on 3 Mar 2026 (https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/on-increases-annual-revenue-by-30-percent-and-forecasts-further-growth/2026030386616): -6.1%. Investor Day reaffirmation plus 2029 targets and buyback: +7.6% (22 Sep 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: FY consensus of $4.33bn sits at the midpoint of the range, so the market assumes about 21% and a Q4 acceleration to about 19% cc. That has to be shown in a promotional US market after Deckers cut its HOKA guide on 23 Oct. If the market doubted the acceleration, FY consensus would sit below the midpoint and the stock would not be up 26% since Investor Day. The sign is a weak lean because 'low-20%' leaves room either way.
findings.independence: The Q2 call commentary (Q3 below Q4, SS27 order book doubled, Cloudsurfer 3 in specialty from October) points to the upside (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/on-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-11/). Jefferies (Konik, $20 PT, 25 Sep 2026, https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/federer-backed-ons-investor-day-doesnt-sway-bearish-analyst/92120842) argues US sell-out softness is demand rather than sell-in. These are two sources pointing opposite ways.

findings.finding: Up to $65m (CHF 53m) of tariff refunds is expected to be booked in Q3 reported gross profit and is excluded from guidance. That is about 5.7% of Q3 sales, or roughly CHF 0.13 a share after tax. Consensus EPS of CHF 0.346 (down 4% YoY) appears to exclude it, so headline EPS and gross margin will look like a large beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no On precedent. The peer precedent: Deckers' fiscal Q2 EPS on 23 Oct 2026 included a $0.28 IEEPA refund benefit, and the stock still fell about 9% on a sales miss and a HOKA guide cut (https://www.sgieurope.com/financial-results/hoka-growth-slows-and-deckers-shares-fall-on-sales-miss/123766.article).
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is public and excluded from the guide. It has no path to the outlook or the multiple, so it can only move the headline EPS print and algorithmic first reads. If the market valued it, the stock would have moved on the 22 Sep disclosure for that reason, and that day's move is attributed to the 2029 targets and the buyback.
findings.independence: Deckers received IEEPA refunds in the same quarter (finviz DECK release, https://finviz.com/news/406824/deckers-brands-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results), which confirms the refund mechanism was paying out in Q3.

findings.finding: The Swiss franc has weakened since the FY CHF range was set. The 11 Aug release put FY26 at CHF 3.47-3.56bn 'at current spot rates'. FXStreet reported the franc at 16-month lows against the dollar on 1 Oct 2026, with USD/CHF about 0.81-0.83 in late September against about 0.80 a year earlier. That compares with an 8-point reported-vs-cc gap in Q2 (13.5% against 21.6%). An unchanged cc guide should therefore translate into a higher CHF range, and Q3 reported growth should sit close to cc growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated on this name. In 2025 a CHF 173m FX hit drove reported net income down 15.9% (https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/on-increases-annual-revenue-by-30-percent-and-forecasts-further-growth/2026030386616) without being the line the stock traded on. On plans to move to USD reporting from as early as 2027 (Investor Day summary, https://quartr.com/events/on-holding-ag-onon-investor-day-2026_oqMIlf0u).
findings.why_not_priced: Most consensus is modelled in USD or cc, so a CHF-reported 'raise' that is pure translation may still produce a positive headline. Sophisticated holders see through it, so it is small. If it were fully modelled, CHF consensus for Q3 would sit visibly above 17% (it is 17.2%, so the read is consistent with FX-neutral).
findings.independence: MarketXLS/FRED series: USD/CHF 0.8282 on 25 Sep 2026 (https://marketxls.com/indicators/usd-to-chf-exchange-rate). This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: Peer: Deckers reported on 23 Oct 2026, after On last spoke. HOKA grew only 6.8% (wholesale +9%, DTC +4%), Deckers cut its FY HOKA guide from low double digits to high single digits, missed revenue (its first fiscal-Q2 miss in at least five years per Piper), and the stock fell about 9%. That points to a soft US premium-running market in the quarter On is reporting and guiding into.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Read-through: On's Q2 Americas wholesale softness (+13.0% cc, everyday running sell-out below plan) coincided with the -20% reaction in August.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: ONON has risen since 23 Oct (from about $33.8 on 1 Nov to $37.07), so the market either did not apply the HOKA read-through or reads HOKA's slowdown as share gain for On. If the read-through were priced, ONON would have fallen with DECK. The share-shift reading weakens this finding, hence the small size.
findings.independence: The fashionunited Deckers Q2 note (https://fashionunited.com/news/business/deckers-brands-reports-q2-revenue-growth-and-appoints-the-realreal-ceo-to-board/2026102375356) is the same event. The opposite evidence on category health is in the next finding.

findings.finding: Peers: the running category itself was strong in the quarter. Nike said running grew double digits in fiscal Q1 to 31 Aug 2026 (release 1 Oct 2026). Adidas Q3 2026 showed running +19%, North America +12% cc, and 'full-price sales' driving growth, with its FY profit guide raised. That is a healthier full-price environment for On's wholesale reset, but also stronger competition in the specialty and max-cushion channel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Public peer prints, which are proxies. They cut both ways (healthier category, more competition), so the net is small.
findings.independence: The Nike FY27 Q1 release (https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results) is a different company and a different source. The Deckers finding above points the other way.

findings.finding: European wholesale partner: Zalando's Q3 2026 (3 Nov) had pro forma GMV +6.1%, a kept 2026 guide, and an explicit bet on sports. EMEA wholesale (On's EMEA was +20.5% cc in Q2) is steady with no distress signal.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy for one partner and is not On-specific, so it is small. It would only matter if EMEA had been the worry, and it was not (management said sell-through outside the Americas was on plan).

findings.finding: Positioning: expectations have been rebuilt into the print. The stock is +40% from the $26.37 post-Q2 low, +26% from the $29.39 Investor Day close, and about +9.7% since 1 Nov ($33.78 to $37.07), with 25-delta skew at -2.18 (calls slightly bid). A Q3 that merely meets a pre-announced 17% and an unchanged FY range faces a sell-the-news risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Investor Day pop the stock kept rising for six weeks. In Aug 2026 a stock that had not run up still fell 20% on a cut, so the run-up is not the main driver of the reaction size.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so the argument is about asymmetry rather than information. The option market leans mildly upside (negative skew), against this finding, so it is sized small. Short interest is about 6% of float with 4.9 days to cover, not crowded.
findings.independence: Simply Wall St, 5 Nov 2026, notes a 5.8% rise with no specific cause (https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/consumer-durables/nyse-onon/on-holding/news/why-on-onon-is-up-58-and-whats-next). The sealed baseline gives run_up_5d 4.36%.

outside_window.finding: Amer Sports (Salomon, Arc'teryx) reports Q3 on 17 Nov 2026, after the window. It pre-raised its Q3 growth guide to 20-22% in September, so it is a premium-sportswear read-through that ONON's trade will not see.

rejected_candidates.detail: The baseline flags cadence_implausible. Only 2026-08-11, 05-12 and 03-03 match dated company releases; the 01-28, 03-25, 04-17 and 05-28 rows are not earnings, and 09-22 was Investor Day. The rebuilt base rate from confirmed prints is +18 (Nov-25), -6.1, -0.6, -20.3.

rejected_candidates.detail: Disagrees with futunn's CHF 931.06m and with the company's ~17% cc guide; the page returned 403, so it cannot be verified. The bar used is the guide plus futunn/EW.

rejected_candidates.detail: The Investor Day summary (quartr) says USD reporting comes from as early as 2027. The claim is unverified, and the reporting-currency mention is folded into the FX finding.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the guidance finding (Q4 implied acceleration) as supporting evidence.

rejected_candidates.detail: Already announced and reacted to on 22 Sep (+7.6%), with no execution disclosure since. It is context for the positioning finding, not a new in-window item.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The mildly call-bid skew and the strong run-up price a constructive print. My small negative tilt (Deckers read-through, Q4 acceleration burden, sell-the-news) cuts against the skew, but only weakly, so p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): the tariff-refund finding is cut from +0.3 to +0.1 because it is excluded from the guide and has no path to the outlook; the Deckers precedent (refund in EPS, stock -9%) is cited.
Lesson 7 (positioning against skew): the sell-the-news finding is cut from -0.8 to -0.6 because the 25d skew (-2.18) leans mildly upside and short interest (about 6%, 4.9 days) is not crowded.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs broad series): the Deckers read-through is cut from -0.6 to -0.5 because the broader Nike/Adidas running series points the other way.

Baseline-history lesson (FPI cadence): the reaction base rate is rebuilt from confirmed releases (+18, -6.1, -0.6, -20.3; median |move| about 12), so abs_move_pct goes from 9.0 to 10.0 and p_up stays at 48.

Lesson 6 (bar): the bar is checked against the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources (futunn CHF and EW USD), so there is no cap. The guidance and FX findings are noted as inside or beside the company's own guided figures.
